headline: Ten days: subs 20→23, views 8,511→11,650 (+37%). Two things reframe everything this week. (1) 95% of a video's lifetime thumbnail impressions arrive in its first 7 days — after that YouTube serves it 1–10 times a day, forever. So packaging is a launch-day decision and retro-fitted thumbnails/retitles are not 'weak', they are unrunnable; the whole retro-packaging experiment has to be retired. (2) A metadata bug hid the channel's single largest asset: the Ep 2 clip pulled 8,840 impressions (more than any other video, 96% of them in 3 days) and converted at 0.42% — ~26 views out of 8,500 — and it never appeared in a single report because the uploads playlist omitted it. Meanwhile Ep 6, the first episode cut under the new retention defaults, is the best on every axis (16.1% avg view, 11.5% still watching at the end vs 3–6.8% everywhere else, and the ONLY episode that doesn't lose half its audience in the first 90 seconds). The edit defaults work; the launch packaging is what's leaking.

production.title: 95% of lifetime impressions land in the first 7 days — packaging must be right AT LAUNCH, and retro-packaging is impossible
production.evidence: Per-video daily impressions from the Reporting API (32 videos published inside the 6/11–7/28 window): first 7 days = 95.1% of all lifetime impressions, after day 7 = 4.9%. Per-video: Ep 2 clip 8,770 of 8,840 impressions (99%) inside 7 days, 96% inside THREE days, then 1–7/day for the next month. Ep 4 OpenUSD clip 3,815 of 3,867 (99%) then 1–9/day. Ep 5 episode 1,438 of 1,712 (84%) then collapses after 7/17. The three videos the last pull targeted for custom thumbnails were already down to 1–2 impressions/day when the experiment was written — the Ep 2 clip got 1 impression on 7/22 and 1 on 7/27, so there was literally nothing left to convert. NOTE: the previous insight ('impressions froze at +15') was a measurement error — reach in channel-data.json is a sum over the ~48 retained daily reports, a SLIDING WINDOW, so diffing it across pulls is invalid.
production.recommendation: Treat title + thumbnail as a hard launch-day gate: they ship with the upload or the video is spent. Never schedule a 'fix the packaging later' task again — instead, pre-write 2–3 title/thumbnail candidates during the edit and pick before publish. The only legitimate retro-action on an old video is re-uploading it as a new asset.
production.status_note: Ep 8 published 7/31 with (per Jackson) title+description verbatim from the draft; whether a custom thumbnail was live at launch is UNVERIFIED (thumbnails aren't dateable via the API — needs a Studio check). Ep 8 has no reach data yet: the report window ends 7/28 and the Reporting API lags ~48 h, so its first-week CTR reads on the next pull (~8/2+). That number is the single most important thing to check next week.

production.title: The channel's biggest asset was invisible: a metadata bug dropped an 8,840-impression video from every report
production.evidence: yt_pull.py enumerated videos from the uploads playlist alone, which returned 59 items but only 58 unique (one duplicate) and silently omitted the public video qwlCzhwirRI ('The US Government AI Rugged Us - Ep 2 Clip', 51 views, 620 s, live and playable, on the brand channel). search(forMine) returned all 59. Its 8,840 impressions — the largest of any video on the channel, 2.4x the runner-up — were dropped on the floor because pull_reach only assigns reach to videos present in the list, and it did so without warning. It also has a full 100-point retention curve that had never been read.
production.recommendation: FIXED this pull: enumeration now unions the uploads playlist with search(forMine) and dedupes, and pull_reach now prints a WARNING for any impressions belonging to an unknown video instead of discarding them silently. The re-pull picked up 59 videos and 11 retention curves (was 58/10). Remaining orphan is UQ6-6zdPL2Q at 13 impressions — a genuinely deleted video, safe to ignore.
production.status_note: Both fixes are in .claude/skills/channel-analytics/scripts/yt_pull.py with the incident documented in a comment so the union isn't 'simplified' back to one source later.

production.title: That hidden video is also the channel's worst packaging failure, and it shows what a failed audition costs
production.evidence: Ep 2 clip: 8,509 impressions in its first 3 days at ~0.31% CTR (~26 views), lifetime 0.42% — against a channel long-form range of 0.68–7.81%. YouTube auditioned it harder than anything else the channel has ever published and then stopped completely (1–7 impressions/day since). Compare 'We Let Claude Gamble Our Money at 20x Leverage' at 3.43% on 6,236 impressions, and the Ep 6 clip at 7.81% on 64. Its 7.4% avg view % means the click that did happen wasn't rewarded either.
production.recommendation: This is the strongest evidence on the channel for the launch-packaging rule above: a big first-week impression allocation is not a second chance, it's the only chance. Re-cut this clip as a NEW upload with a real hook title and thumbnail rather than trying to revive the existing one.

production.title: Shorts→episode funnel is still the highest-leverage unfixed thing, and it's now 8 clips behind
production.evidence: Shorts: 10,447 views → 630 watch-minutes and 4 subs (0.038 subs/100 views, 0.06 min/view). Long-form: 881 views → 3,409 watch-minutes and 13 subs (1.476 subs/100 views, 3.87 min/view). Long-form converts a viewer to a subscriber ~39x better per view and produces 5.4x the watch-time off a tenth of the views. Shorts traffic grew +2,642 views this period but only +129 watch-minutes. RELATED_VIDEO is wired (confirmed 7/21) and is moving, but slowly: 86→97 views, 206→254 watch-minutes. SUBSCRIBER traffic is the quality source at 546 views → 1,171 minutes.
production.recommendation: Work the funnel checklist on Ep 8's 8 clips as they go public Jul 31–Aug 7 — related video → episode, pinned comment with the ?t= link (all 8 timestamps are already in episodes/ep8/segment-times.md), end screens. RELATED_VIDEO views/watch-min is the metric to judge it by next pull.
production.status_note: Related-video wired on all shorts through Ep 7. Ep 8's 8 clips uploaded 7/31 scheduled-private; their checklist is untouched and pinned comments can't be set until each goes public.

production.title: The cold-open handoff is the single biggest edit leak — and Ep 6 proves it's fixable
production.evidence: Every episode loses the majority of its audience in the first 60–90 seconds: Ep 1 −52.2pp (0:50→1:41), Ep 2 −55.1pp (0:39→1:19), Ep 3 −71.8pp (0:45→1:30), Ep 4 −54.0pp (0:44→1:28), Ep 5 −47.7pp (0:36→1:13), Ep 7 −56.7pp (0:29→0:58). Ep 6 is the sole exception at −26.9pp (0:33→1:07) — roughly half the leak — and it is also the best episode on every downstream axis: 16.1% avg view, 11.5% still present at the end (vs 3.0–6.8% for every other episode), early-window vs_typical 0.64 (vs 0.13–0.43 elsewhere), and late-episode vs_typical 0.95. Ep 6 was the first episode cut under the retention-informed edit defaults.
production.recommendation: Keep the Ep 6 shape and attack what's left of the handoff: the drop is at the seam where the cold open ends and the welcome/title begins. On Ep 9, cut the teaser straight into segment 1 with no welcome block at all and compare the 0:30–1:30 loss against Ep 6's −26.9pp.
production.status_note: Defaults are in podcast-video-edit SKILL.md and shipped on Ep 6/7/8. Ep 8's curve isn't available yet (published today) — it's the confirmation case.

production.title: Clip length drives completion; the subject drives views — the 10–20s default holds
production.evidence: Short avg view % by duration: 12s→58.7%, 14s→55.1%, 15s→81.7%, 20s→41.1%, 21s→96.5%, against 25s→48.6%, 27s→35.5%, 38s→38.8%. Completion falls off past ~20s while view counts track the topic, not the length.
production.recommendation: Keep cutting 10–20s verticals; Ep 8's batch is 9–19s and compliant. Stop treating a 30s+ setup as viable for verticals.

production.title: Episode launches are now bracketed by a live clip queue — keep it, and pre-check for collisions
production.evidence: Ep 6 launched into a dead queue (77 impressions / 21 views in its first 3 days) and still recovered to 432 impressions at 3.24% CTR once clips started. Daily views show the clip queue working: 7/25–7/28 ran 655 / 836 / 231 / 410 views against 8–13/day the week before.
production.recommendation: Keep the daily 2 PM PT cadence. Standing pre-flight: check the PREVIOUS episode's clip schedule for a same-day collision before setting a new batch's publishAt — Ep 8's lead clip and Ep 7's freestyle short both landed on Jul 31 2 PM PT and the lead was moved to 6 PM.

recording.title: Don't ship a solo episode as the main feed item
recording.evidence: Ep 7 (Jackson solo) is the worst episode on the channel on every measure: 0.68% CTR on 1,029 impressions, 200 s avg view duration, 6.8% avg view %, 3.3% still watching at the end, and −56.7pp in the first 29 seconds followed by another −16.7pp by 1:28. Early-window vs_typical 0.31. For contrast Ep 6 (full panel) holds 11.5% to the end at 16.1%.
recording.recommendation: When hosts are out, ship a short-form or a clip package instead of a full solo episode — or bring a guest. The three-host dynamic is the format's product.

recording.title: The ≤8-minute explainer cap held again — Ep 7 broke it by 4x and paid
recording.evidence: Ep 7's vibe-coding block ran 12:29→48:00 — about 72% of the episode in one segment. Its retention shows −10.0pp at 15:43→16:13 (16.7%→6.7%, vs_typical 0.20) right as the block settles in, and never recovers. Every episode's steepest mid-show cliff sits inside a long explainer.
recording.recommendation: Hard-cap explainers at 8 minutes on the mic and tie each to live stakes or a personal story; if a topic can't be, it's a clip, not a segment.

recording.title: AI bits and live stakes are the retention spine — the evidence got stronger
recording.evidence: Ep 6's late-episode vs_typical is 0.95 (near channel-typical) and it finishes at 11.5% — its structure front-loaded the AI-clone segment and opened Perp of Fortune at 18:26 rather than Ep 5's 27:08. Ep 5's own steepest mid-show drop is −6.8pp at 37:30, after its retainer had already been spent.
recording.recommendation: Keep one retainer bit (Perp of Fortune / confession / AI bit) inside the first 10 minutes, every episode. Ep 8 has the Ripple-guy confession at 34:51 — that's late; move the next one earlier.

recording.title: Check-in discipline: the fix shipped on Ep 8, now verify it
recording.evidence: Ep 5 lost −9.1pp at 1:50→2:27 during the gamer-thumb/check-in saga (vs_typical 0.29). Ep 8 moved check-in out of the top of the show to 18:34 as a mid-show palate cleanser, with the marquee at 2:06.
recording.recommendation: Judge this against Ep 8's retention curve next pull: the 1:50–2:30 region should no longer show a distinct drop, and 18:00–19:00 should not crater.
